name: Pinacoteca de São Paulo
funding: Maintainer B3. São Paulo state via APAC. Lei Rouanet. Master sponsors Bradesco, InfinitePay, Itaú, Vivo, Chanel. Gold sponsors include Equinor, Ultra, Bloomberg, J.P. Morgan, Motiva.

name: Pivô
funding: Federal Cultural Incentive Law (Lei Rouanet), philanthropic patron circle, international cultural foundations. Independent Brazilian non-profit audit.

name: Sesc São Paulo
funding: 2023 revenue R$3.44bn: R$2.70bn (78%) from the compulsory levy on commerce, services and tourism firms, R$209M from services, R$495M financial income.

name: Sofia City Art Gallery
funding: Sofia Municipality funds yearly acquisitions, resumed in 2007. Partners listed: Ministry of Culture, America for Bulgaria Foundation, Aurubis Bulgaria, Institut français and Goethe-Institut. No budget is published.

name: Laongo Granite Sculpture Symposium
funding: Burkina Faso's culture ministry organises it and pays professional artists' fees, flights and stay, per its 2024 call for applications. No other funder is named.

name: FESPACO
funding: About 1.3-1.5bn FCFA executed in 2025 (~US$2.3M), nearly 80% from the Burkina state; EU 195M FCFA, plus the UN, OIF, LONAB lottery and telecoms.

name: Musée National du Burkina Faso
funding: State museum (EPSCT) with 30,000+ visits Jan-Oct 2024, funded by the culture ministry plus Ouagadougou commune, Agence Faso Mɛbo and unnamed company donors.

name: Sa Sa Art Projects
funding: Artist-run. Funding found: an online artist auction (2022), documenta fifteen money for a community studio, and a Rei Foundation partnership from 2018 to 2024. No funder list is published.

name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum
funding: Run by Cambodia's Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts, which lists it among its institutions. Foreign adults pay $5 and Cambodians enter free, the museum states.

name: Bandjoun Station
funding: Small artist-run centre opened 2013, paid for by Barthélémy Toguo, his coffee plantations and the Amis de Bandjoun Station association.

name: doual'art
funding: Its site footer credits support from Arts collaboratory, Brot für di welt, ZFD Ziviler friedensdienst, CPS Peace Work Africa and SUPSI.

name: Musée National du Cameroun
funding: State museum under the Ministry of Arts and Culture; €1M modernisation from AFD via debt-swap C2D (2019-24), Phase 2 2025-27, run by Expertise France.
